questions.q: What are the four real parts that make up a Service Portal Widget (`sp_widget`)?
options: Portal, Theme, Page, and Layout
GlideRecord, GlideAjax, Business Rule, and UI Policy
HTML Template, CSS/SCSS, Server Script, and Client Controller
Homepage, Catalog Page, Knowledge Page, and Ticket Page
questions.explain: Portal/Theme/Page are the site-level layers from Lesson 26; a widget itself is HTML Template + CSS + Server Script + Client Controller.

options: getValue() is required to activate the incident record
Pushing gr directly would delete the incident
A raw GlideRecord object can't cross from the server-side script to the client — only plain values (strings, numbers, arrays of plain objects) can be attached to data
GlideRecord objects are automatically converted to HTML on the client with no extra code needed
questions.explain: data must hold plain, serializable values; getValue()/getDisplayValue() extract those from the GlideRecord before it's exposed to the client.

questions.q:
What does the `ng-repeat="inc in c.data.incidents"` attribute do in this HTML Template fragment? ```html
  • {{inc.number}} — {{inc.short_description}}
    • ```
options: Deletes every incident in the array once rendered
Renders one `<li>` element for each item in the `c.data.incidents` array, with `{{ }}` interpolating each item's fields
Runs a server-side Business Rule once per incident
ng-repeat is a CSS class with no functional behavior
questions.explain: ng-repeat is the AngularJS directive that loops markup over an array, producing one rendered element per item.

options: `c` is a server-side-only variable that the HTML Template can never reference
It sets up the "controller as" alias `c` used in the HTML (as `c.data`, `c.openIncident`), and `openIncident` is a plain function the template's `ng-click` calls to navigate to the ticket page
`openIncident` runs automatically on page load with no user interaction required
It deletes the current scope and replaces it with a new GlideRecord
questions.explain: The controller-as pattern aliases `this` to `c`; `c.openIncident` is wired to the HTML's `ng-click="c.openIncident(inc)"`.

questions.q: What is the correct order for building a new Service Portal widget, per this lesson?
options: Drag the widget onto a Page before writing any of its four parts
Write the Client Controller first, since it's the only part that matters
Write the Server Script first to know what the data looks like, then the HTML Template to render it, then the Client Controller to wire up interactive behavior
Write the CSS first, since styling must exist before any data or markup
questions.explain: The Server Script defines the shape of data the HTML Template depends on, and the Client Controller wires behavior the template calls into.
